in my limited but recent experience... this is how I'm perceiving things out of 7 interviews (1 recruiter, 1 phone screen and 5 on-site):
- 3 no-go's - you're likely done, no offer.
- 2 no-go's - could be over with no offer OR could be sent to the hiring committee where you may be extended an offer, but very likely down-leveled.  HC could even decide to re-interview one or more portions before deciding.
- 1 no-go - won't be over, but you will be sent to the hiring committee who then decides what level your offer would be including down-leveled, at level or up-leveled (although unlikely).  Could also be re-interviewed.
- 0 no-go - sent to hiring committee and will likely get an offer at level or even up-leveled (likely)
Sounds reasonable

tl;dr Google won't halt for 2 weeks. We overhired way too many people and very likely it will be evolved into a series of reorg and layoff. Q2 earning will most likely be dismal as well (my guess, if you have a hiring freeze before the Q2 earning, what do you think?). Please prep for the worst (if you don't get an offer, suggest move on).

Explanation: 
attrition + PIP + lay off = one-year overhire + inflow of new hires 

Google leadership's original strategy is to overhire and reshuffle the workforce by pushing out those experienced low performers out (by natural attrition in the hot market) and overhire mixed-quality talents and then use GRAD to select the top performers and PIP those mediocres (that's why you have so many downlevels and lowballs). The similar strategy was applied at Amazon. Now with the economic downturn, the attrition part is gone but to make up that part, Google needs to cut off the inflow (hiring freeze) and rely more heavily on PIP (likely max 8% this cycle).

The worse part is not to bring the balance i.e. balance out inflow and outflow to maintain a stable state. The goal, not hard to guess, is probably to bring back to early COVID level because we hired so many people with 0 increase in scope. That means attrition + pip alone won't likely be sufficient to do the job. It will eventually lead to lay off.

And so, companies will do a hard stop on the thing they can control quickly - headcount and hiring.
The job market now has an interesting dynamic that supply is starting to exceed demand which wasn't the case two months ago.
Very qualified candidates are being laid off and hence the market is changing to be an employers market.
